body.statement: For every adjacent maternal-smoking intensity contrast \(c_j=e_{j+1}-e_j\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{adj}}\), compute \(N_Bv_j\) with \(N_B=I_{K^{2}}-D^{-1}B(B^{\mathsf T}D^{-1}B)^{+}B^{\mathsf T}\). The recovered augmented conditional Gram matrix \(G_j^{\mathrm{aug}}(X)\) satisfies \(\operatorname{rank}\{G_j^{\mathrm{aug}}(X)\}\leq\operatorname{rank}\{G(X)\}+1\), and the observable condition \(P_X[\operatorname{rank}\{G_j^{\mathrm{aug}}(X)\}=\operatorname{rank}\{G(X)\}+1]>0\), equivalently \(P_X\{\Lambda_j(X)>0\}>0\), certifies \(c_j^{\mathsf T}Q\phi\neq0\) and strict variance reduction for that dose step. As a supporting consequence, \(c_j^{\mathsf T}(V_{\mathrm{raw}}-V_{\mathrm{eff}})c_j=E_P\{(c_j^{\mathsf T}Q\phi)^2\}=E_P\{\Lambda_j(X)\}>0\); more generally, \(c^{\mathsf T}(V_{\mathrm{raw}}-V_{\mathrm{eff}})c=E_P\{(c^{\mathsf T}Q\phi)^2\}\) for every \(c\in\mathbb R^K\).
body.justification: The conditional residual-energy diagnostic can be estimated from recovered cells and the same Gram solve, so strict gain for each adjacent exposure step is empirically certifiable rather than assumed.
body.gap: Categorical product-bridge validity and the abstract projection formula do not provide an observable criterion for deciding which scientifically prespecified adjacent smoking-intensity contrasts receive a nonzero correction.
body.consumer: It lets the maternal-smoking analyst report, for every neighboring pair of exposure bins, whether canonicalization yields a genuine efficiency gain.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(c_j\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{adj}}\), and abbreviate \(v=v_j\), \(b=b_v\), and \(e=E\{(N_Bv)^2\mid X\}\).  The augmented matrix is the conditional Gram matrix of \((h^{\mathsf T},N_Bv)^{\mathsf T}\); adjoining one vector increases rank by at most one.  If \(a\in\ker G\), then \(E\{(a^{\mathsf T}h)^2\mid X\}=0\), so \(a^{\mathsf T}h=0\) conditionally and \(a^{\mathsf T}b=0\).  Thus \(b\perp\ker G\), or \(b\in\operatorname{range}G\).  Block elimination with \(G^+\) therefore gives
\[
\operatorname{rank}G_j^{\mathrm{aug}}
=\operatorname{rank}G+\mathbf 1\{e-b^{\mathsf T}G^+b>0\}. \tag{32}
\]
Indeed, the generalized Schur complement is
\[
\begin{aligned}
e-b^{\mathsf T}G^+b
&=E\!\left[\{N_Bv-h^{\mathsf T}G^+b\}^2\mid X\right]\\
&=E\{(c_j^{\mathsf T}Q\phi)^2\mid X\}
=\Lambda_j(X)\geq0.
\end{aligned} \tag{33}
\]
The second equality follows from linearity of \(Q\) and the definition of the cell vector \(v_j\).  Equations (32)--(33) prove equivalence of the positive-probability rank increase, \(P_X\{\Lambda_j>0\}>0\), and \(c_j^{\mathsf T}Q\phi\ne0\) in \(L^2(P)\).

Since \(Q\) is an orthogonal projection, \(Q\phi\) and \((I-Q)\phi=\phi^{\mathrm{eff}}\) are orthogonal coordinatewise.  Therefore, for every \(c\in\mathbb R^K\),
\[
c^{\mathsf T}(V_{\mathrm{raw}}-V_{\mathrm{eff}})c
=E\{(c^{\mathsf T}Q\phi)^2\}. \tag{34}
\]
For \(c=c_j\), combining (33) and (34) gives the stated equality with \(E\{\Lambda_j(X)\}\), and strict positivity holds exactly under the displayed observable certificate.
